text: Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that enables systems to learn from data.
Deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers to model complex patterns.
Natural language processing allows computers to understand and generate human language.
Computer vision enables machines to interpret and understand visual information.
Reinforcement learning trains agents to make decisions through trial and error.
Transformer architectures revolutionized NLP with attention mechanisms.
Convolutional neural networks excel at image classification tasks.
Recurrent neural networks process sequential data like text and time series.
Transfer learning allows models trained on one task to be applied to another.
Generative adversarial networks learn to create realistic synthetic data.
Support vector machines find optimal hyperplanes for classification.
Decision trees partition data using feature-based rules.
Random forests combine multiple decision trees for robust predictions.
Gradient boosting iteratively improves predictions by correcting errors.
Clustering algorithms group similar data points without labels.
Dimensionality reduction projects high-dimensional data to lower dimensions.
Bayesian inference updates beliefs based on observed evidence.
Graph neural networks operate on graph-structured data.
Attention mechanisms allow models to focus on relevant input parts.
BERT uses bidirectional training to improve language understanding.
GPT models generate coherent text through autoregressive prediction.
Word embeddings represent words as dense vectors in semantic space.
Semantic search retrieves documents based on meaning rather than keywords.
Vector databases store and query high-dimensional embedding vectors.
Retrieval augmented generation combines retrieval with language generation.
Knowledge graphs represent facts as interconnected entity relationships.
Federated learning trains models on distributed data without centralizing it.
Differential privacy adds noise to protect individual data in datasets.
Adversarial examples fool neural networks with imperceptible perturbations.
Model distillation transfers knowledge from large to smaller models.
Quantization reduces model precision to decrease memory and computation.
Pruning removes redundant parameters from neural networks.
Neural architecture search automates the design of neural network structures.
Meta-learning trains models to quickly adapt to new tasks with few examples.
Few-shot learning generalizes to new tasks with minimal training data.
Zero-shot learning classifies inputs into classes not seen during training.
Active learning selects the most informative samples for labeling.
Semi-supervised learning leverages unlabeled data alongside labeled samples.
Self-supervised learning creates training signals from the data itself.
Contrastive learning learns representations by contrasting similar and different samples.
Multi-task learning trains models to perform multiple related tasks simultaneously.
Ensemble methods combine predictions from multiple models for better accuracy.
Hyperparameter optimization searches for the best model configuration.
Cross-validation estimates model performance on unseen data.
Regularization techniques prevent overfitting in machine learning models.
Batch normalization stabilizes training by normalizing layer activations.
Dropout randomly deactivates neurons during training to prevent overfitting.
Adam optimizer adapts learning rates based on gradient history.
Learning rate scheduling adjusts the learning rate during training.
Early stopping halts training when validation performance stops improving.
